properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (root-cause skill, 2026-10-24): no design-time choice could read as supported, because a premise's truth reused the delivery line (a requirement holds when delivered or met, a capability when realized and checked) for a design choice whose grounds are its owner's accepted intent; the class recorded for closure on 2026-09-29, recurring in inference.rs
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-24, on the Shop sample trial (flo2.io 671a764fa790c030, reflow2 0.91.0; hub fact:shop-sample-trial-friction-2026-10-24, items A1 and B9).

① OBSERVED: 19 accepted design choices (dec:sample-choice-*), each concluded by one step. Every chain read `unknown` (proof_status unproven); premise rows said "not delivered, and its status (accepted) says neither met nor dropped". loop_status listed all 19 under "WHAT HAS LOST ITS REASON NOW" with 74 uncited premises; detect_gaps raised "19 conclusion(s) claim more than the steps that conclude them support". Not affected: accepted decisions, constraints and measured findings, which read `holds`.

② PRECEDENT: inference.rs own_truth reads a Requirement as taken_as_given, delivered by the roll-up or `met`, else unknown, and never reads `accepted`; the module doc says the values come "from what reflow2 ALREADY computes for each type" (bfb064b8a, 2026-10-14). req:a-choice-that-rests-on-checkable-premises-is-recorded-as-a-chain item 1 (2026-10-16) named "a met requirement". capture-intent's routing table (a42269d89, 2026-10-18) named "an accepted requirement", contradicting the code and add_inference's own description ("a requirement delivered or met"). Same class: fact:root-cause-closure-cannot-read-design-done-because-traceability-was-bound-to-the-delivery-line-2026-09-29.

③④⑤ CANDIDATES, each with the measurement that could refute it: (C1) the requirement premise reads delivery, never acceptance: confirmed in code, but the only blocker in 5 of 19 chains; (C2) served guidance promised accepted requirements would count: not refuted (capture-intent); (C3) the agents built chains reflow2 did not intend: partly confirmed (7 chains use Artifacts as premises, 1 Interfaces, about 5 unrealized Capabilities, none of which carries a truth); (C4) the design's own state: about 9 chains rest on Alex's requirements, still `proposed`, which read unknown honestly under any reading; (C5) an honest way to cite intent already exists: `taken_as_given` makes the premise hold but detect.rs is_a_statement then stops asking for the requirement's satisfier, hiding real gaps; citing the governing accepted Decision works but no guidance names it. C2 and the hub's own brief predict the same chains and were not told apart.

⑥ CLASS: a verdict defined for one purpose reused for another because it was the only computation there was. A premise's truth answered "is this established in the built world?" for every intent record except a Decision (acceptance) and a Constraint (holds unless violated), so a choice resting on stated intent could never read supported before it was built. The closure fix of 2026-09-29 stayed in closure.rs; the inference module reused the delivery line again two weeks later. A requirement record carries two propositions, "X is required" and "X holds in the system", and the premise did not say which it used.

DECIDED: dec:a-premise-says-whether-it-rests-on-intent-or-delivery (Anthony, 2026-10-24). Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018ibUbMKCS1yK5W17cncp9P
